currentContext.expansion: FY26 was focused on productivity improvements to maximise utilisation of plant capacities already installed, while FY27 will see an enhancement in capacity in both the two-wheeler and the OHT segments through ongoing Board-approved investments in manufacturing capacity, productivity improvement and technology upgradation. During FY26 the Board approved additional capital expenditure of Rs 210.00 crores for the Uttarakhand Expansion Project at UKD-II, aimed at expanding the Company's manufacturing capacity. Subsequently, at its meeting held on 27th May 2026, the Board approved further capital expenditure of Rs 220.00 crores, comprising Rs 110.00 crores for the Two-Wheeler plant and Rs 110.00 crores for the Off-Highway Tyre plant, towards capacity expansion at the manufacturing facilities located at Vellaripatti, Madurai. Capital expenditure during FY26 itself amounted to Rs 106.09 crores. On the market side, the acquisition of Super Grip in the USA was integrated into the Company's larger global outreach during FY26, the global channel-partner network is being enhanced and Company personnel are being placed in global markets. On energy infrastructure, the Company completed a 5 MWp group-captive solar plant for Uttarakhand plant #1, uses 100% biomass fuel for steam generation at the Uttarakhand plant, and invested for a 5.92% equity stake in Navia Two Power Private Limited to purchase solar power under the Group Captive mode. The Company was granted a Structured Package of Assistance from SIPCOT comprising a capital subsidy aggregating Rs 75.00 crores receivable in 12 equal instalments, a Green Industry Incentive of Rs 1.00 crore and a training subsidy of Rs 68.40 lakhs. Manufacturing is carried out at Madurai in Tamil Nadu and Rudrapur in Uttarakhand, with design facilities in India and Italy.

themes.title: Auto OEM cycle - CV replacement & PV premiumization
themes.need: GST 2.0 rate rationalization plus an aged CV fleet still frames the replacement cycle, but Q1FY27's real signal is 2W OEMs EXPANDING margin through a commodity shock. TVSMOTOR sold 1.63mn units (+28%) on INR 13,896cr revenue (+38%) while lifting EBITDA margin 30bps to 12.8% having absorbed a ~4% commodity shock with only ~1.5% of price increase (CARE upgraded it AA+ to AAA), and committed 2W capacity from 6.8mn to 8.3mn by Q4FY27. BAJAJ-AUTO set volume/revenue/EBITDA records with margin at 20.9% (+110bps) through ~4.5% commodity inflation AND ~10% of volume lost to a ransomware shutdown, with EV now 30% of domestic revenue at double-digit EBITDA and Chetak EBITDA-positive - a scaled, profitable EV second engine. Commercial mobility is electrifying fastest: TVSMOTOR's 3W EV penetration crossed 40% for the first time. ASHOKLEY's all-time-high CV volumes (220k units, MHCV share 30.8%) carry the CV leg with defence + Switch EV optionality; TMCV/TMPV/SMLMAH/ESCORTS on CV/tractors; APOLLOTYRE/JKTYRE/BALKRISIND/MRF on tyres.
themes.driver: Capacity commissioning against demand (TVSMOTOR 2W to 8.3mn by Q4FY27, BAJAJ-AUTO 7m to 9m+ units); 3W/2W EV penetration inflection; GST-2.0 price-cut demand, aged-fleet replacement and festive 2W/PV.
